summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of systolic heart failure, ischemic cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and obesity, was admitted for acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbated by missing two days of torsemide during travel. He presented with worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, 10 kg weight gain, and lower extremity edema. Treatment included IV furosemide, which led to a weight reduction from 140 kg to 132 kg. His symptoms improved, though mild fluid overload persisted. Due to his preference for early discharge, he was transitioned to oral torsemide 160 mg daily, with increased hydralazine for blood pressure control. His creatinine rose to 2.3, consistent with baseline, likely due to diuresis. He was discharged home with compression stockings, strict medication adherence counseling, and a plan for close outpatient follow-up to monitor renal function and adjust diuretic therapy as needed.
